The Last Waltz

Magnus Blackmoor, the Lord of Light and elected leader of Anchester, holds a gala for his cabinet and the richest families in the city. Colonel Standard, head of the Special Police, attends in dress uniform. He ran the serum program that turned soldiers into monsters, and he carries one of the Pale Journals, the stolen occult books the serum came from. He means to hand it in private to Lady Adela Blackmoor, who is secretly the Clairvoyant. Outside, the city's poor crowd the gates with forged invitations; inside, student radicals plan a protest. No one knows that Zeshagu, the enemy besieging the city, has landed five dragonborn assassins on the island to take that Journal.

Timeline

Fifteen years ago. A collector had the Pale Journals, books of forbidden lore, stolen from a temple in Sai Abbadon and brought to Anchester.

Two years ago. The enemy powers of Zeshagu and Sous Terreborgue took Sai Abbadon. A year later their dragons and warships put Anchester under siege.

Six months ago. The Special Police, under Colonel Standard, began dosing volunteer soldiers with a serum made from the Journals.

Weeks ago. At Paschendale the dosed soldiers became monsters and killed friend and foe alike. The city was told it was a victory.

Days ago. The players saved Freitman Bay, the last soldier of Paschendale, and captured Dr. Pemberton, whose shadow is the killer called the Smiling Man. Standard kidnapped Bay's pregnant wife, Claudia, and delivered her to a figure called the Clairvoyant.

Yesterday. Hazel Attwater's underground broadsheet named the Clairvoyant as the power behind the experiments. Her source says the Clairvoyant will be at the Lord of Light's gala. Evelyn Ridgely, Claudia's friend, heard Standard will be there too.

Today. The gala. The players go to find Standard and the Clairvoyant.

Episode Structure

A society ball that ends in a massacre. The players come to the gala to find Colonel Standard and the Clairvoyant. They do not know who the Clairvoyant is, and this episode does not tell them. DM only: the Clairvoyant is Lady Adela Blackmoor. Nothing in this episode reveals or hints at it.

The evening runs as a series of disruptions, each louder than the last: gate-crashers at the door, a stink bomb, red paint thrown over the host and his wife. In the confusion Standard slips away to hand over his Journal and is interrupted.

Then the dragonborn come through the skylights. Four slaughter the guests while the fifth hunts Standard and kills him before he can talk. The players end the night with his Journal and an iron gate key. The Journal reveals what the Clairvoyant wants, to become a God King with an outsider's power, but not how. The key leads to Episode Nine.

What Each Doom Spend Does

Mythos Disadvantage. Disadvantage on one roll: the hand shakes, the mind stalls.

Murphy's Law. A glass breaks, a heel snaps, a door sticks.

Everyone's a Suspect. A guest the players trusted repeats what they said to the wrong person. One guest from the Who's Who table turns cold.

Paper-Thin Disguise. A servant or Special Policeman looks twice at one player. The next Deception or Stealth check in company has disadvantage.

Cut Off. A door is locked, a corridor is crowded, a footman bars the way. The players must go around.

Sound the Alarm! Plain-clothes Special Police escort the players toward the Foyer unless they talk their way free.

Enemy Reinforcements. Another pair of plain-clothes Special Police joins the room; once the attack begins, a dragonborn arrives instead.

Activate one Dread Ability. Trigger a Dread Insight already held by a player.

Map Locations

1. Gates and Drive. Wrought-iron gates on the Crown Ring road. The crowd of gate-crashers presses here, and the Watch, the city's ordinary police, holds the line, barely.

2. Grand Foyer. Marble stair down to the drive. Percival Towson, the house butler, keeps the guest ledger at a lectern inside the doors.

3. Offices. Two private offices off the Foyer. The Blackmoors change here after the paint.

4. Ballroom. Quartet, dance floor, the main crowd. The dragonborn assassins strike here first, in Scene 8.

5. Sitting Room. A hired spiritualist reads palms by candlelight. Quiet enough for a private word.

6. Conservatory. Glass, palms, dim light. A favoured place for an assignation.

7. Baths. Guests' retiring rooms. The student radicals hide their stink bomb here, in Scene 4.

8. Dining Room. The buffet. The champagne came in on Rupert Hurlock's blockade-runner. Ogden Pryce, the Harbormaster, guards the food.

9. Drawing Room. Lady Augusta Westminster, President of the Upper Chamber, holds court with senators and their wives.

10. Library. Locked cases, leather chairs, a private door to the Terrace.

11. Great Hall. The overflow crowd. Most of the cabinet stands here with Hollis Vane, the Magistrate General.

12. Kitchen. Footmen, steam, noise. The service stair starts here.

13. Servants' Wing. Service passages to every room. Aldith Denman pays the servants to tell her who comes and goes.

14. Terrace. French doors from the Dining Room, Drawing Room and Library. Archibold Gayle, Commander of Air Defense, smokes here.

15. Gardens. Hedge maze, pool, pavilion. Dark, and open to the sky.

Using This Table

The guests are the Lord of Light, his cabinet and their spouses, old money, new money, and the three heirs of the Osgood crime family, who are fighting over the dead matriarch's empire. Run Scenes 3 through 7 from this table. Each player picks a guest; the DM answers from the third column and adds 1 to the Doom Counter for every guest pressed hard enough to remember the player's face. Lady Blackmoor reads as nothing more than a gracious host. Play her that way every time.

Choosing the Handoff

In Scene 5 Colonel Standard slips away to hand his Pale Journal to Lady Blackmoor in a private room. The DM picks the room: the Library (10), the Conservatory (6) or the Offices (3). When the attack comes in Scene 8, that room is where the Black Dragonborn Assassin goes first. Towson, the butler, opened the room for the Colonel and tells anyone who tips him or outranks him. Nothing the players can learn tonight ties Lady Blackmoor to the Journal; to them she is a host who stepped out for air.

The Clarion Society, late afternoon. ~20 min

A rack of borrowed evening clothes stands by the fire. On the table lie a guest list, a pressed invitation and a plan of Crown Ring.

What's Happening. The players prepare at the Clarion Society, their base. They know two things. Evelyn Ridgely, the young woman who hid with Claudia Bay, heard Colonel Standard say he would wear his dress uniform to the gala. Hazel Attwater, who prints the underground broadsheet The Worker, says her source puts the Clairvoyant on the guest list. Claudia herself will not be there. Evelyn helps the players dress and tells them who matters.

Clues. Evelyn names her parents, the Ridgelys, as friendly faces inside. Hazel sends word that she has printed several hundred forged invitations and handed them to the city's poor, and that some university radicals who read her broadsheet mean to "make a statement."

Interactables. A genuine invitation, obtained through the Ridgelys. Forged invitations from Hazel. Evening dress. Weapons must be small enough to hide; the house searches anything larger at the door.

Scene Flow. Let the players choose how they enter: as the Ridgelys' guests, on forged cards, as hired staff, or over the wall. Each choice sets up Scene 2. A DC 14 Intelligence (History) check recalls that the Special Police, Standard's secret force, run security for the Lord of Light, not the Watch.

Gates and Drive (1), dusk. ~20 min

Carriages stand three deep on the gravel drive. Beyond the iron gates, a crowd in threadbare coats holds printed invitations up to the lamplight.

What's Happening. Twenty to forty of the city's poor wave Hazel's forged invitations and shout their names. The constables of the Watch, who answer to Hollis Vane, the Magistrate General, are overwhelmed. Special Police in plain clothes watch from the steps and pick out faces.

Clues. Vane, at the gate, is embarrassed and honest: the Special Police run the house tonight. A gate-crasher who is helped will say that university students took a bundle of the forgeries.

Scene Flow. Getting through takes one check by the approach the players chose:

  • Success. The players are inside without being marked.
  • Failure. They are inside, but a plain-clothes Special Policeman remembers them; the Doom Counter rises by 1.

Players who help the crowd gain Vane's goodwill for the rest of the night.

Grand Foyer (2) and Ballroom (4), 8 PM. ~30 min

A quartet plays under the chandeliers. The Lord of Light and his wife greet each guest at the foot of the stair, and the room is full of masks, medals and diamonds.

What's Happening. Magnus and Lady Adela Blackmoor receive their guests. Colonel Standard, in black dress uniform, stands at the Lord's shoulder for the first hour and speaks with him privately at least twice. The cabinet ministers and the three Osgood heirs work the room.

Clues. Use the Who's Who at the Gala table for any guest the players approach. A DC 16 Wisdom (Insight) check on Standard notices he keeps one hand near a slim leather case under his arm. A DC 18 Wisdom (Perception) check catches him checking his watch against the clock over the stair, twice in ten minutes.

Scene Flow. Approaching Standard directly earns a cold refusal and a nod to his plain-clothes men; the Doom Counter rises by 1. Let the players mingle until the room settles, then run Scene 4.

Ballroom (4), 9 PM. ~15 min

A glass vial shatters on the parquet near the quartet. The smell reaches the dancers a moment later.

What's Happening. University radicals who came in on Hazel's forged invitations set off a stink bomb from the Baths (7). Guests flee to the Terrace and the Great Hall. The Special Police move on the students.

Clues. A student caught before the Special Police reach them will say the paint is still coming. One will admit the invitations came from Hazel Attwater; most will not.

Scene Flow. The players may help, hinder or ignore the students. Shielding a student from the Special Police gains a friend in Scene 6; handing one over gains a plain-clothes officer's trust. In the confusion, ask each player where they are standing; the answers matter in Scene 5.

Anywhere in the house, 9:30 PM. ~25 min

The quartet starts again. The Lord of Light laughs too loudly near the fire, and the place at his shoulder is empty.

What's Happening. Standard has slipped away to hand his Pale Journal to Lady Blackmoor in private, in the room the DM chose (see Choosing the Handoff). She follows five minutes later; no player sees her go.

Clues. Old Lady Salisbury saw him leave, and by which door. Towson knows which room was opened. The servants Aldith Denman pays know the rest. A DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) check on the service stair finds Standard's route.

Scene Flow. If the players reach the room, they find Standard alone, waiting; he orders them out. Do not let them hear the handoff. If they linger, Scene 6 begins before Lady Blackmoor arrives.

Ballroom (4), 10 PM. ~20 min

A young man in a borrowed tailcoat steps out of the crowd with a pot in his hands. Red paint arcs across the dance floor.

What's Happening. One of the students throws red paint over the Lord of Light and Lady Blackmoor, who has just returned to the Ballroom. More students try to paint the guests. Wystan Aldous, the hot-tempered Osgood heir, sets his bodyguards swinging. The Special Police wade in.

Clues. The scuffle interrupts the handoff: Standard still has the Journal. A DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check sees him return to the edge of the Ballroom, the leather case still under his arm.

Scene Flow. Treat the scuffle as a short skirmish against Revolutionary Students and Osgood Bodyguards. No one dies here unless the players want it. Players who protect the Blackmoors earn the Lord's gratitude and a place near him for Scene 7.

Offices (3), 10:30 PM. ~15 min

Footmen carry basins of water across the Foyer. Behind a closed office door, the Lord of Light is shouting for a clean shirt.

What's Happening. The Blackmoors withdraw to the Offices to change. Standard waits outside to try again. This is the players' last window to reach him.

Clues. Standard, if cornered here, will not speak of the Journal. A DC 20 Charisma (Intimidation or Persuasion) check gets one sentence: "You have no idea who you are dealing with." He will say no more. Nothing he says points to Lady Blackmoor.

Scene Flow. End the scene when the players commit to a course, or when the Doom Counter reaches 12. Either way, Scene 8 begins.

Ballroom (4) and the handoff room, 11 PM. ~60 min

The skylights above the Ballroom burst inward. Five winged shapes drop through the falling glass, blades already drawn.

What's Happening. Zeshagu, the enemy besieging Anchester, has sent five dragonborn assassins to take Standard's Journal. Getting them onto the island cost Zeshagu a thousand lives; there is no second team. Each assassin is named for the colour of its scales. Red, the leader, takes White, Blue and Green through the Ballroom to cause panic. Black, the ninja, goes straight for Standard and the Journal.

The Massacre. At the end of each round, each of the four Ballroom assassins that no player is fighting kills one guest. Work down the Massacre Track. The Blackmoors are still in the Offices and never die here. At the end of the fight there should be a lot of dead nobles.

Standard's Death. Black reaches Standard first, wherever he is, and kills him before the players can get anything out of him about the Journals, the Clairvoyant or Claudia. If the players are with Standard, Black still reaches him: it turns invisible (Veil of Rot), teleports through the shadows to his side (Shadow Step), and kills him with a single strike. Standard dies.

The Book. Black does not get it. Standard had the Journal sewn into the lining of his tunic. Black searches the leather case, finds it empty, and turns on whoever is closest. Red signals the withdrawal when any assassin falls or after five rounds, and the survivors flee into the night sky.

Clues. On Standard's body: the Pale Journal, sewn into his tunic (a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check, or automatic if the body is searched); an iron gate key on his watch chain. Nothing on him names Lady Blackmoor.

Scene Flow. Hollis Vane and Archibold Gayle fight beside the players. The Special Police try to take Standard's body; let the players decide whether to stop them. The Blackmoors emerge from the Offices only after the dragonborn are gone.

Running the Attack

Use the Dragonborn Assassins on the Horrors page. All five act on Initiative 10. Give each player a moment of choice in the first round: save the nobles in front of them, or run for Standard. They cannot do both.

Outcome Ladder.

  • Total success. The players hold the Journal and the key, drove off the dragonborn with few nobles dead, and kept the Special Police from Standard's body.
  • Mixed. The players hold the Journal and the key, but many nobles died and the Special Police took Standard's body.
  • Total failure. Every outcome still leaves the Journal and the key with the players. The cost is in the dead: Vane, Gayle or the Ridgelys among them, and a city that blames the players.

Rewards. Standard's Pale Journal. An iron gate key from Standard's watch chain. The goodwill of anyone the players saved.

Insight Cue. Reading the Journal is a Mythos exposure: the reader rolls to resist and fails automatically, and gains this plot Insight: the reader learns that someone in Anchester means to become a God King by taking the power of an outsider into themselves. The Journal does not say how, or who.

Foreshadowing. The iron key opens the gate of a walled building somewhere in the city; Episode Nine begins when the players find it. Lady Blackmoor writes a warm note of thanks to every guest who survived, the players included.

Threads and Dead Ends.

  • The gate key. The live thread. It opens the gate of the building the players assault in Episode Nine.
  • The Journal. Tells the players what is wanted (a God King made from an outsider's power), not how and not who.
  • The student radicals. A dead end. They know the forgeries and the paint, nothing about the Clairvoyant.
  • Merewyn Osgood's warehouses. A side thread. Standard's men watched them; with Standard dead, no one says why.
  • The Special Police. If they took Standard's body, they claim the dragonborn killed him for his rank. They know nothing else.
